name: GITM (Ghost in the Minecraft)
what_evolved: Context memory & prompts (text-based knowledge and memory); LLM weights are frozen (GPT used via API). Evolves a text memory of accumulated successful action-list summaries + a text knowledge base from Minecraft wikis/recipes.
skill_as_artifact: Yes. Successful plans are recorded and summarized as reusable text-based memory entries ('common solutions') that serve as reference for future planning.
skill_encoding: Natural language (text-based knowledge from Minecraft Wiki/recipes; text summaries of successful structured-action sequences). Not a formal graph, despite 'knowledge graph' phrasing.
skill_granularity: Sub-task workflow: LLM Decomposer breaks goals into a sub-goal tree; LLM Planner produces sequences of structured actions (explore/approach/mine/equip/smelt...) for each sub-goal.
how_method: No gradient/RL model training. Frozen GPT via API. Learns by recording & summarizing successful action lists into text memory as reusable references (self-generated successful-trajectory demonstrations / in-context exemplars). Closest to imitation_demonstration from own successful rollouts + in-context memory reuse.
learning_signal_source: Success/failure trajectories: LLM Interface returns execution feedback (success/failure + inventory changes); only successful plans are summarized and stored.
reward_granularity: Hybrid: per-action execution feedback (success/failure, inventory deltas) plus sub-goal outcome (goal achieved or not).
learning_paradigm: Online, on-policy (agent generates its own plans/trajectories and accumulates memory during live task execution).
when_evolve: Intra-test-time (online during task execution), with memory carrying over across sub-goals/attempts to enhance future planning.
trigger: Event-triggered: success events store/summarize a plan into memory; failure events trigger plan revision by the LLM Planner.
library_structure: Text-based: (1) a static text knowledge base sourced from Minecraft Wiki and in-game recipes; (2) a flat, growing text memory of summarized successful action lists.
retrieval_method: LLM is fed relevant text knowledge/memory as reference context for planning (generation-as-retrieval / semantic context selection). [uncertain: exact retrieval/ranking mechanism not detailed in paper]
validation: Execution-based: the LLM Interface verifies each structured action against real environment observations (success/failure, inventory state).
error_correction: Self-revision: execution failures are fed back to the LLM Planner, which iteratively corrects/refines the action plan.
test_env: Minecraft (open-world, long-horizon crafting/survival tasks, ObtainDiamond benchmark, full Overworld technology tree).
backbone_model: GPT-3.5 (text-davinci) for LLM Decomposer and LLM Planner; LLM Interface uses hardcoded keyboard/mouse scripts.
metrics: success_rate (ObtainDiamond), generalization (full technology-tree coverage), sample_efficiency / training cost (CPU vs GPU days), skill_library_growth (learning curve from text-memory accumulation).
key_results: 67.5% ObtainDiamond success rate (+47.5% over OpenAI VPT SOTA of 20%); first agent to obtain all 262 Overworld items (100% tech tree vs 30% for all prior methods combined); ~10,000x more efficient (2 days on a 32-core CPU, no GPU) vs 6,480 GPU-days (VPT) and 17 GPU-days (DreamerV3).
limitations: transferability (Minecraft-specific text knowledge and hardcoded low-level interface scripts); scalability (depends on LLM reasoning quality and API cost; structured action set is hand-designed); limited to text-based observations rather than raw pixels.
